requirements.subject: ent:ttcn3-language
requirements.canonical: The TTCN-3 language IS providing a number of predefined basic types.
requirements.original: TTCN-3 supports a number of predefined basic types.

requirements.subject: ent:basic-type
requirements.canonical: The basic types IS including integer, boolean and string types as well as TTCN-3 specific types such as `verdicttype`.
requirements.original: These basic types include ones normally associated with a programming language, such as integer, boolean and string types, as well as some TTCN-3 specific ones such as verdicttype.

requirements.subject: ent:structured-type
requirements.canonical: A structured type such as a record type, set type or union type CAN be constructed from basic types.
requirements.original: Structured types such as record types, set types and union types can be constructed from these basic types. enumerated types are specific structured types being constructed of enumerated values.

requirements.subject: ent:enumerated-type
requirements.canonical: An enumerated type IS a specific structured type constructed of enumerated values.
requirements.original: Structured types such as record types, set types and union types can be constructed from these basic types. enumerated types are specific structured types being constructed of enumerated values.

requirements.subject: ent:anytype
requirements.canonical: The `anytype` IS the union of all known types and the address type defined within a TTCN-3 module.
requirements.original: The special data type anytype is defined as the union of all known data types and the address type defined within a TTCN-3 module.

ambiguity.issue: 'known data types' is used; the glossary term is 'known types'.

requirements.subject: ent:anytype
requirements.condition: a value or template of type anytype is used in a specific module context
requirements.canonical: In a value or template of type `anytype`, only the known types of the specific module context SHALL be accessible.
requirements.original: In any specific module context, only the known types can be accessed in a value or template of type anytype.

requirements.subject: ent:configuration-type
requirements.canonical: The special configuration types `address`, `port` and `component` MAY be used to define the architecture of the test system.
requirements.original: Special types associated with test configurations such as address, port and component may be used to define the architecture of the test system (see clause 21).

requirements.subject: ent:default-type
requirements.canonical: The special type `default` MAY be used for default handling.
requirements.original: The special type default may be used for the default handling (see clause 20.5).

requirements.subject: ent:ttcn3-language
requirements.canonical: The TTCN-3 language IS providing the simple basic types `integer`, `float`, `boolean` and `verdicttype`.
requirements.original: TTCN-3 supports the following basic types:

requirements.subject: ent:integer-type
requirements.canonical: The `integer` type IS a type with distinguished values which are the positive and negative whole numbers, including zero.
requirements.original: a) `integer: a type with distinguished values which are the positive and negative whole numbers, including` zero:

requirements.subject: ent:integer-value
requirements.canonical: An integer value SHALL be denoted by one or more digits.
requirements.original: Values of integer type shall be denoted by one or more digits; the first digit shall not be zero unless the value is 0; the value zero shall be represented by a single zero.

requirements.subject: ent:integer-value
requirements.canonical: The first digit of an integer value notation SHALL NOT be zero unless the value is 0.
requirements.original: Values of integer type shall be denoted by one or more digits; the first digit shall not be zero unless the value is 0; the value zero shall be represented by a single zero.

requirements.subject: ent:integer-value
requirements.canonical: The integer value zero SHALL be represented by a single zero.
requirements.original: Values of integer type shall be denoted by one or more digits; the first digit shall not be zero unless the value is 0; the value zero shall be represented by a single zero.

requirements.subject: ent:float-type
requirements.canonical: The `float` type IS a type to describe floating-point numbers and special float values.
requirements.original: b) `float: a type to describe floating-point numbers and special float values:`

requirements.subject: ent:float-value
requirements.canonical: A floating-point number IS in general defined as <mantissa> × <base>^<exponent>, where the mantissa is a positive or negative integer, the base a positive integer and the exponent a positive or negative integer.
requirements.original: In general, floating point numbers can be defined as:<mantissa> × <base>[<exponent>], where <mantissa> is a positive or negative integer, <base> a positive integer (in most cases 2, 10 or 16) and <exponent> a positive or negative integer.

requirements.subject: ent:float-value-notation
requirements.canonical: The TTCN-3 floating-point value notation IS restricted to the base 10.
requirements.original: In TTCN-3, the floating-point number value notation is restricted to a base with the value of 10.

requirements.subject: ent:float-value-notation
requirements.canonical: A float value CAN be expressed in two forms of value notation: the decimal notation and the exponent notation.
requirements.original: Floating point values can be expressed by using two forms of value notations:

requirements.subject: ent:float-value-notation
requirements.canonical: The decimal float value notation IS a sequence of digits containing a dot, e.g. 1.23 (123 × 10^-2), 2.783 or -123.456789.
requirements.original: the decimal notation with a dot in a sequence of numbers like, 1,23 (which represents 123 × 10[-2]), 2,783 (i.e. 2 783 × 10[-3]) or -123,456789 (which represents -123 456 789 × 10[-6]); or

ambiguity.issue: The text says 'with a dot' but the examples are written with a comma (1,23); reading 1 chosen since the text and the TTCN-3 grammar use a dot.
readings: The decimal float value notation IS a sequence of digits containing a dot (e.g. 1.23).
The decimal float value notation IS a sequence of digits containing a comma (e.g. 1,23).

requirements.subject: ent:float-value-notation
requirements.canonical: The exponent float value notation IS two numbers separated by `E`, where the first number specifies the mantissa and the second specifies the exponent, e.g. 12.3E4 or -12.3E-4.
requirements.original: by two numbers separated by E where the first number specifies the mantissa and the second specifies the exponent, for example 12.3E4 (which represents 123 × 10[3]) or -12.3E-4 (which represents -123 × 10[-5]).

requirements.subject: ent:float-value-notation
requirements.canonical: The mantissa in the TTCN-3 float value notation MAY be a decimal number as well as an integer.
requirements.original: NOTE 1: In contrast to the general definition of float values, the mantissa of in theTTCN-3 value notation, beside integers, allows decimal numbers as well.

requirements.subject: ent:special-float-value
requirements.canonical: The special values of the `float` type IS `infinity` (positive infinity), `-infinity` (negative infinity) and `not_a_number`.
requirements.original: The special values of the float type consist of infinity (positive infinity), -infinity (negative infinity) and the value not_a_number.

requirements.subject: ent:special-float-value
requirements.canonical: The value `-not_a_number` SHALL NOT be used.
requirements.original: NOTE 2: `-not_a_number (i.e. minus not a number) is not to be used.`

ambiguity.issue: A NOTE cannot impose a requirement; unclear whether '-not_a_number' is a compile-time error or merely discouraged. Reading 1 chosen as the most likely intent.
readings: The value `-not_a_number` SHALL NOT be used (a tool rejects it).
The value `-not_a_number` SHOULD NOT be used (it is equivalent to `not_a_number` and only discouraged).

requirements.subject: ent:boolean-type
requirements.canonical: The `boolean` type IS a type consisting of two distinguished values.
requirements.original: c) `boolean: a type consisting of two distinguished values:`

requirements.subject: ent:boolean-value
requirements.canonical: A boolean value SHALL be denoted by `true` or `false`.
requirements.original: Values of boolean type shall be denoted by true and false.

requirements.subject: ent:verdicttype
requirements.canonical: The `verdicttype` IS a type for use with test verdicts consisting of 5 distinguished values.
requirements.original: d) `verdicttype: a type for use with test verdicts consisting of 5 distinguished values.

requirements.subject: ent:verdict
requirements.canonical: A `verdicttype` value SHALL be denoted by `pass`, `fail`, `inconc`, `none` or `error`.
requirements.original: Values of` verdicttype shall be denoted by pass, fail, inconc, none and error.
